findings.source: UniswapInterfaceMulticall.sol:30-36 for (...) { (address target, uint256 gasLimit, bytes memory callData) = ...; uint256 gasLeftBefore = gasleft(); (bool success, bytes memory ret) = target.call{gas: gasLimit}(callData); uint256 gasUsed = gasLeftBefore - gasleft(); returnData[i] = Result(success, gasUsed, ret); }
findings.issue: The GAS read that gives gasLeftBefore is executed inside the loop, right before each call (disassembly: GAS at 0x158 after the loads of calls[i], GAS at 0x1c1 after the call, then SUB), but the text hoists it to the first line of the function (_1 = gas_remaining, even before the calldata checks). The text therefore reports, for every call i, the gas used since the function entry instead of the gas used by call i.
findings.rule: GAS is not a pure expression: its value changes with every instruction, so a GAS read must never be hoisted, merged (CSE) or moved across other instructions, in particular out of a loop or across a call; bind each read to a fresh variable at its own position.
findings.verified: pancxx disasm (GAS opcodes only at 0x158 and 0x1c1, both in the loop body); the execution checks do not catch it because gas-dependent outputs are not compared

findings.source: returnData = new Result[](calls.length); return (blockNumber, returnData) (ABI encoding)
findings.issue: The allocation of the Result[] array of structs is a rotated loop (P3), and the return encoding is a 'while True' whose exit branch is the function's return with a length still containing mem[64].
findings.rule: Un-rotate 'if n: B; while n - 1: B' into 'while n: B'; print the exit branch of a 'while True' after the loop; fold mem[64] to the base it was last set from.

notes: All 3 ABI functions reviewed in full (getCurrentBlockTimestamp, getEthBalance, multicall). The source loop is 'while s < _67' (75); implicit loops: the validated abi.decode of Call[] (26), the rotated Result[] allocation (63, P3), the callData copy (83) and the ABI encoding of the results (119/133) (P7). The same treatment of GAS as a pure value is visible in c00465 (fulfillRandomWords' startGas printed as a bare gas_remaining in the payment formula).
summary: Small and mostly readable, but the gasleft() taken before each call is hoisted out of the loop to the function entry, so the text computes a cumulative gasUsed where the bytecode computes per-call gas.
